title: Rank Athena-fixing requests ahead of feature work within a priority tier
summary: Retry of job 20261114-041129-dwmx (dispatched, never verified, no findings, no candidate changes): within the same effective priority tier, `Plan::build_with` orders steward/Hestia fix requests (root-cause, repeated-failure, blind-spot, gate-review) before feature and content items, so `athena plan` and `athena drain` stop starving them. Goal: the owner's filed steward requests run; audience: the owner running `athena plan`/`drain`.

defaults_applied.how: Criteria check the plan and drain order, not that a flag exists.
New unit and drain tests; cargo test, clippy and fmt must pass.
The rule goes in a new appended docs/decisions.md entry.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Job 20261114-041129-dwmx was dispatched and never verified; it recorded no findings and no candidate changes, so there is nothing to keep or fix. This retry starts from the base and reuses its deliverables and out_of_scope unchanged.

Code survey: crates/athena-core/src/plan.rs: `Plan::build_with` (about line 692) holds items, computes `effective_priorities`, then in a loop keeps ready items at the best effective tier and orders them with `ready.sort_by_key(|(age, e)| (e.rung, *age))` (line 783). `PlanEntry` (line 147) has no fix flag. crates/athena-cli/src/drain.rs: `Drain::prepare` calls `Plan::build_improving`/`build_capped`, and approved work items become entries via `proposal_priority` and `role_priority` (about lines 4254-4380). The order is measured directly through `Plan::build_with` output. No record or data file is added, so `check_record_file`/`AnyRecord` do not apply; the change adds no refusal rule.

Term tier: a priority tier is the effective priority level (urgent, high, normal, low) from `effective_priorities`; the fix-first key applies only among ready items already at the best tier, after dependencies.

Fix definition: an entry counts as a fix when it comes from a steward or Hestia work item of kind root-cause, repeated-failure, blind-spot or gate-review. It is carried as a new PlanEntry field set where entries are built from work items in drain.rs and reading/topics.rs, defaulting false. Steward website and study content requests are not fixes.
Existing code: crates/athena-core/src/plan.rs (`Plan::build_with`, `PlanEntry`), crates/athena-cli/src/drain.rs, crates/athena-cli/tests/drain.rs and docs/decisions.md are extended, not replaced.

acceptance_criteria.text: A new unit test in crates/athena-core/src/plan.rs builds a plan with an older normal feature entry and a newer normal fix entry, both ready; the plan order puts the fix entry first. Run `cargo test -p athena-core`.

A unit test shows an urgent or high feature item still precedes a normal fix item, and an item depending on another still follows it, so the fix flag never overrides priority or dependencies. Run `cargo test -p athena-core`.
A unit test shows a steward website or studies content request is not flagged as a fix and keeps its age-ordered place behind older items of its tier. Run `cargo test -p athena-cli`.

A drain test in crates/athena-cli/tests/drain.rs (or a unit test in crates/athena-cli/src/drain.rs) has an approved steward blind-spot or repeated-failure work item and an older normal feature request; the drain dispatches the steward job first. Run `cargo test -p athena-cli`.
The plan.rs module doc 'Order' paragraph says fix items come first inside a priority tier, and the diff shows the `ready.sort_by_key` key in `Plan::build_with` placing fix entries before others.
docs/decisions.md gains a new appended entry stating the rule with a Provenance bullet citing the owner's request; no existing entry changes. CHANGELOG.md records the job.
`cargo test`, `cargo clippy` and `cargo fmt --check` pass on the final tree, per Athena's recorded checks on the same tree.

out_of_scope: Changing how steward or Hestia raise or classify work items
Changing priority levels, urgent/high caps, or the `athena priority` command
Editing existing entries in docs/decisions.md or anything under records/
Changes to athena.toml, defaults.toml or CI workflows
departures: Slightly higher cost and lower pass chance than the reference: the change touches the core plan ordering and drain together, and the previous attempt never got verified.
hard_reason: It changes the plan order rule that the run pipeline and drain use to choose which job runs next.
